{
  "cells": [
    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "metadata": {
        "id": "aWci6ur8YzxP"
      },
      "source": [
        "# Data Mining Lab - Book Recommender System on a Medallion Data Lake\n",
        "\n",
        "**Name:** Safiya Nasir &nbsp;&nbsp; **Roll no:** LCI2023053\n",
        "\n",
        "Pipeline: **raw CSVs -> Bronze (untouched copy) -> Silver (cleaned) -> Gold (model-ready) -> Item-based collaborative filtering recommender.**\n",
        "\n",
        "Dataset: Book-Crossing (`BX-Users`, `BX-Books`, `BX-Book-Ratings`).\n"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "metadata": {
        "id": "ydZvn9oVYzxQ"
      },
      "source": [
        "import os, glob, zipfile, urllib.request, html, string\n",
        "from collections import defaultdict\n",
        "from datetime import datetime, timezone\n",
        "\n",
        "import numpy as np\n",
        "import pandas as pd\n",
        "import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n",
        "from scipy import sparse\n",
        "from sklearn.neighbors import NearestNeighbors\n",
        "\n",
        "pd.set_option('display.max_columns', 50)\n",
        "pd.set_option('display.width', 200)\n",
        "CURRENT_YEAR = datetime.now().year"
      ],
      "execution_count": 29,
      "outputs": []
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "metadata": {
        "id": "66ZRA5QSYzxR"
      },
      "source": [
        "## Step 1 - Set up the data lake and build the Bronze layer\n",
        "\n",
        "Create the folders `bronze/`, `silver/`, `gold/` (plus `raw/` for the downloaded zip)."
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "metadata": {
        "colab": {
          "base_uri": "https://localhost:8080/"
        },
        "id": "hrFj630DYzxS",
        "outputId": "395994b5-ae0d-4a55-fcad-7caa567b6d4a"
      },
      "source": [
        "for folder in ['raw', 'bronze', 'silver', 'gold']:\n",
        "    os.makedirs(folder, exist_ok=True)\n",
        "print(sorted(os.listdir('.')))"
      ],
      "execution_count": 30,
      "outputs": [
        {
          "output_type": "stream",
          "name": "stdout",
          "text": [
            "['.config', 'bronze', 'gold', 'raw', 'sample_data', 'silver']\n"
          ]
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "metadata": {
        "colab": {
          "base_uri": "https://localhost:8080/"
        },
        "id": "YFAdk_PgYzxS",
        "outputId": "37d46f2b-e0d0-497c-85b3-5b4bb93c5c46"
      },
      "source": [
        "# Download and unzip the raw Book-Crossing files\n",
        "URL = 'https://cdn.freecodecamp.org/project-data/books/book-crossings.zip'\n",
        "zip_path = 'raw/book-crossings.zip'\n",
        "if not os.path.exists(zip_path):\n",
        "    # the server returns 403 to Python's default downloader, so identify as a browser\n",
        "    req = urllib.request.Request(URL, headers={'User-Agent': 'Mozilla/5.0'})\n",
        "    with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as resp, open(zip_path, 'wb') as f:\n",
        "        f.write(resp.read())\n",
        "with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_path) as z:\n",
        "    z.extractall('raw')\n",
        "    print(z.namelist())"
      ],
      "execution_count": 31,
      "outputs": [
        {
          "output_type": "stream",
          "name": "stdout",
          "text": [
            "['BX-Book-Ratings.csv', 'BX-Books.csv', 'BX-Users.csv']\n"
          ]
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "metadata": {
        "colab": {
          "base_uri": "https://localhost:8080/"
        },
        "id": "IrF0aaCfYzxT",
        "outputId": "833540da-5567-49a7-875f-22107c4d38d1"
      },
      "source": [
        "def find_file(suffix):\n",
        "    hits = [p for p in glob.glob('raw/**/*.csv', recursive=True) if p.endswith(suffix)]\n",
        "    assert hits, f'No file ending in {suffix} found in raw/'\n",
        "    return hits[0]\n",
        "\n",
        "books_file   = find_file('Books.csv')\n",
        "users_file   = find_file('Users.csv')\n",
        "ratings_file = find_file('Ratings.csv')\n",
        "print(books_file, users_file, ratings_file)"
      ],
      "execution_count": 32,
      "outputs": [
        {
          "output_type": "stream",
          "name": "stdout",
          "text": [
            "raw/BX-Books.csv raw/BX-Users.csv raw/BX-Book-Ratings.csv\n"
          ]
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "metadata": {
        "id": "2lPyMVeJYzxT"
      },
      "source": [
        "The files are **semicolon-separated** and encoded in **Latin-1 (ISO-8859-1)**, not UTF-8.\n",
        "For Bronze we read every column as text (`dtype=str`) so nothing is converted or \"fixed\" — Bronze is an exact copy of the source.\n",
        "Lines that the CSV parser physically cannot split are reported (`on_bad_lines='warn'`) and skipped."
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "metadata": {
        "colab": {
          "base_uri": "https://localhost:8080/"
        },
        "id": "Uan730gXYzxT",
        "outputId": "31a86628-a866-488a-bf08-e0eb17c555bf"
      },
      "source": [
        "def read_raw(path):\n",
        "    return pd.read_csv(path, sep=';', encoding='latin-1', dtype=str,\n",
        "                       quotechar='\"', on_bad_lines='warn')\n",
        "\n",
        "ingestion_time = datetime.now(timezone.utc)\n",
        "bronze = {\n",
        "    'books':   read_raw(books_file),\n",
        "    'users':   read_raw(users_file),\n",
        "    'ratings': read_raw(ratings_file),\n",
        "}\n",
        "for name, df in bronze.items():\n",
        "    df['ingestion_timestamp'] = ingestion_time\n",
        "    df.to_parquet(f'bronze/{name}.parquet', index=False)\n",
        "    print(f'{name:8s} {df.shape}  -> bronze/{name}.parquet')"
      ],
      "execution_count": 33,
      "outputs": [
        {
          "output_type": "stream",
          "name": "stderr",

    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "metadata": {
        "id": "Vykf30ylYzxT"
      },
      "source": [
        "## Step 2 - Explore the Bronze data (EDA)\n",
        "\n",
        "We read the tables back **from the Bronze layer** (not from the CSVs)."
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "metadata": {
        "colab": {
          "base_uri": "https://localhost:8080/"
        },
        "id": "e4cTg2AVYzxU",
        "outputId": "9012eeed-6800-47ff-d4c1-5729475aa62f"
      },
      "source": [
        "b_books   = pd.read_parquet('bronze/books.parquet')\n",
        "b_users   = pd.read_parquet('bronze/users.parquet')\n",
        "b_ratings = pd.read_parquet('bronze/ratings.parquet')\n",
        "\n",
        "for name, df in [('BOOKS', b_books), ('USERS', b_users), ('RATINGS', b_ratings)]:\n",
        "    print(f'===== {name}: shape {df.shape} =====')\n",
        "    print(pd.DataFrame({'dtype': df.dtypes.astype(str), 'missing': df.isna().sum()}))\n",
        "    print('duplicate rows:', df.drop(columns='ingestion_timestamp').duplicated().sum(), '\\n')"
      ],

        "id": "rPDRhQRNYzxU"
      },
      "source": [
        "**2.1 Shape / types / missing values:** Books has 271,360 rows, Users 278,858 rows, Ratings 1,149,780 rows. All columns are text in Bronze; `Age` has 110,762 missing values (≈39.7 %), Books has a few missing authors/publishers, and the 3 image-URL columns are not needed.\n",
        "-> *In Silver:* cast IDs/age/rating/year to numbers, drop the image-URL columns, drop duplicate rows."
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "metadata": {
        "colab": {
          "base_uri": "https://localhost:8080/",
          "height": 747
        },
        "id": "QbLYgviyYzxU",
        "outputId": "e31e2606-5459-4199-cc8c-f5618524766c"
      },
      "source": [
        "rating_num = pd.to_numeric(b_ratings['Book-Rating'], errors='coerce')\n",
        "rating_counts = rating_num.value_counts().sort_index()\n",
        "print(rating_counts)\n",
        "print(f\"\\nRatings equal to 0: {(rating_num == 0).sum():,} \"\n",
        "      f\"({(rating_num == 0).mean() * 100:.1f}% of all ratings)\")\n",
        "\n",
        "rating_counts.plot(kind='bar', title='Distribution of Book-Rating (Bronze)', xlabel='rating', ylabel='count')\n",
        "plt.show()"
      ],
      "execution_count": 36,
      "outputs": [

    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "metadata": {
        "id": "GGNSXwAJYzxU"
      },
      "source": [
        "**2.2 Ratings:** 62.3 % of all ratings are **0**, which means \"implicit / no explicit rating\". The explicit ratings (1-10) are skewed towards high values (most common: 8).\n",
        "-> *In Silver:* remove all 0 ratings and keep only 1-10."
      ]
    },

      "cell_type": "code",

        "colab": {

        },

      },
      "source": [

        "id": "5UiUQaaoYzxV"

      "source": [
        "**2.3 Ages and years:** Age ranges from 0.0 to 244.0 (impossible values: 882 users under 5 and 366 over 100). Publication year has 4,618 rows equal to 0, 11 in the future and 3 non-numeric values (rows where the columns were shifted).\n",
        "-> *In Silver:* ages < 5 or > 100 -> null, then fill with the median age; year 0 / future / non-numeric -> null."
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "metadata": {
        "colab": {
          "base_uri": "https://localhost:8080/",
          "height": 970
        },
        "id": "aDtG9TATYzxV",
        "outputId": "824afe0d-b31e-4fcc-af98-e03e1a060c8d"
      },
      "source": [
        "explicit = b_ratings[rating_num.between(1, 10)]\n",
        "per_user = explicit['User-ID'].value_counts()\n",
        "per_book = explicit['ISBN'].value_counts()\n",
        "\n",
        "print('Explicit ratings per USER:'); print(per_user.describe().round(2))\n",
        "print('\\nExplicit ratings per BOOK:'); print(per_book.describe().round(2))\n",
        "\n",
        "thresholds = [1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100]\n",
        "print('\\nHow many users / books have at least k explicit ratings:')\n",
        "print(pd.DataFrame({'users': [(per_user >= k).sum() for k in thresholds],\n",
        "                    'books': [(per_book >= k).sum() for k in thresholds]}, index=thresholds).rename_axis('k'))\n",
        "\n",
        "fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 4))\n",
        "per_user.clip(upper=50).plot(kind='hist', bins=50, ax=ax[0], title='Ratings per user (clipped at 50)', logy=True)\n",
        "per_book.clip(upper=50).plot(kind='hist', bins=50, ax=ax[1], title='Ratings per book (clipped at 50)', logy=True)\n",
        "plt.show()"

    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "metadata": {
        "id": "b927tNVmYzxV"
      },
      "source": [
        "**2.4 Ratings per user / book:** The median user has only 1.0 explicit rating(s) and the median book 1.0; only 7,334 users and 5,645 books have 10 or more ratings (long-tail distribution).\n",
        "-> *In Silver:* keep only users and books with at least **10** ratings (justified in Step 3)."
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "metadata": {
        "colab": {
          "base_uri": "https://localhost:8080/"
        },
        "id": "x4-1ValMYzxV",
        "outputId": "dc5650cc-bd33-45c1-a44f-053905c3b8ac"
      },
      "source": [
        "def sparsity_report(df, user_col, book_col, label):\n",
        "    n_u, n_b, n_r = df[user_col].nunique(), df[book_col].nunique(), len(df)\n",
        "    density = n_r / (n_u * n_b) * 100\n",
        "    print(f'{label}: {n_u:,} users x {n_b:,} books = {n_u * n_b:,} possible pairs; '\n",
        "          f'{n_r:,} ratings -> density {density:.5f}%  (sparsity {100 - density:.5f}%)')\n",
        "\n",
        "sparsity_report(b_ratings, 'User-ID', 'ISBN', 'All ratings     ')\n",
        "sparsity_report(explicit,  'User-ID', 'ISBN', 'Explicit (1-10) ')"
      ],
      "execution_count": 40,
      "outputs": [
        {
          "output_type": "stream",
          "name": "stdout",
          "text": [
            "All ratings     : 105,283 users x 340,556 books = 35,854,757,348 possible pairs; 1,149,780 ratings -> density 0.00321%  (sparsity 99.99679%)\n",
            "Explicit (1-10) : 77,805 users x 185,973 books = 14,469,629,265 possible pairs; 433,671 ratings -> density 0.00300%  (sparsity 99.99700%)\n"
          ]
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "metadata": {
        "id": "Zd3MaQEnYzxV"
      },
      "source": [
        "**2.5 Sparsity:** Only 0.00300 % of all possible user-book pairs have an explicit rating - the matrix is more than 99.99 % empty.\n",
        "-> *In Silver/Gold:* filter to active users / popular books and store the matrix as a **sparse** matrix."
      ]
    },

      "source": [
        "## Step 3 - Clean the data and build the Silver layer"

        "log = []   # keep a record of how many rows each cleaning step removes\n",
        "def note(step, df):\n",
        "    log.append((step, len(df)))\n",
        "    print(f'{step:55s} {len(df):>10,}')"

        "id": "5mP83Q8qYzxV"
      },
      "source": [
        "### 3a. Users - duplicates, age fix, split Location"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "metadata": {
        "colab": {
          "base_uri": "https://localhost:8080/",
          "height": 260
        },
        "id": "4R95X4nBYzxV",
        "outputId": "8b52a718-554b-46dd-a255-48b77907418a"
      },
      "source": [
        "users = (b_users.drop(columns='ingestion_timestamp')\n",
        "                .rename(columns={'User-ID': 'user_id', 'Location': 'location', 'Age': 'age'}))\n",
        "note('users: bronze', users)\n",
        "users = users.drop_duplicates()\n",
        "users['user_id'] = pd.to_numeric(users['user_id'], errors='coerce')\n",
        "users = users.dropna(subset=['user_id']).astype({'user_id': 'int64'})\n",
        "users = users.drop_duplicates(subset='user_id')\n",
        "note('users: after removing duplicates / bad ids', users)\n",
        "\n",
        "# Age: impossible values -> null -> median\n",
        "users['age'] = pd.to_numeric(users['age'], errors='coerce')\n",
        "users.loc[(users['age'] < 5) | (users['age'] > 100), 'age'] = np.nan\n",
        "median_age = users['age'].median()\n",
        "print('Median valid age used to fill nulls:', median_age)\n",
        "users['age'] = users['age'].fillna(median_age).round().astype(int)\n",
        "\n",
        "# Location \"city, state, country\" -> 3 columns\n",
        "users['location'] = (users['location'].fillna('').str.lower()\n",
        "                     .str.replace(r'\\s+', ' ', regex=True).str.strip())\n",
        "parts = users['location'].str.split(',')\n",
        "users['city']    = parts.str[0]\n",
        "users['state']   = parts.str[1]\n",
        "users['country'] = parts.apply(lambda p: p[-1] if len(p) >= 3 else None)\n",
        "\n",
        "placeholders = {'', 'n/a', 'na', 'none', 'null', 'unknown', '.', ',', '-', '?'}\n",
        "for col in ['city', 'state', 'country']:\n",
        "    users[col] = users[col].str.strip().str.strip('.\"\\'').str.strip()\n",
        "    users[col] = users[col].where(~users[col].isin(placeholders))\n",
        "\n",
        "users.head()"
      ],
      "execution_count": 42,
      "outputs": [
        {
          "output_type": "stream",
          "name": "stdout",
          "text": [
            "users: bronze                                              278,858\n",

    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "metadata": {
        "id": "57EsUW5sYzxV"
      },
      "source": [
        "### 3b. Books - duplicates, years, text cleaning, drop image URLs"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "metadata": {
        "colab": {
          "base_uri": "https://localhost:8080/",
          "height": 242
        },
        "id": "MCPDdz45YzxV",
        "outputId": "8d99f1d3-c6ef-425b-fbc3-5d4858123bce"
      },
      "source": [
        "books = (b_books.drop(columns=['ingestion_timestamp', 'Image-URL-S', 'Image-URL-M', 'Image-URL-L'], errors='ignore')\n",
        "                .rename(columns={'ISBN': 'isbn', 'Book-Title': 'title', 'Book-Author': 'author',\n",
        "                                 'Year-Of-Publication': 'year', 'Publisher': 'publisher'}))\n",
        "note('books: bronze', books)\n",
        "books = books.drop_duplicates()\n",
        "\n",
        "def clean_text(s):\n",
        "    s = s.astype('string')\n",
        "    s = s.map(lambda x: html.unescape(x) if isinstance(x, str) else x, na_action='ignore').astype('string')\n",
        "    s = s.str.replace(r'\\s+', ' ', regex=True).str.strip()\n",
        "    return s.mask(s == '')\n",
        "\n",
        "books['isbn']      = clean_text(books['isbn']).str.upper()\n",
        "books['title']     = clean_text(books['title']).map(string.capwords, na_action='ignore').astype('string')\n",
        "books['author']    = clean_text(books['author']).str.title()\n",
        "books['publisher'] = clean_text(books['publisher']).str.title()\n",
        "\n",
        "books = books.dropna(subset=['isbn', 'title']).drop_duplicates(subset='isbn')\n",
        "note('books: after removing duplicates / missing isbn or title', books)\n",
        "\n",
        "# Year: non-numeric, 0 or future -> null\n",
        "books['year'] = pd.to_numeric(books['year'], errors='coerce')\n",
        "books.loc[(books['year'] == 0) | (books['year'] > CURRENT_YEAR), 'year'] = np.nan\n",
        "books['year'] = books['year'].astype('Int64')\n",
        "\n",
        "books.head()"
      ],
      "execution_count": 43,

    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "metadata": {
        "id": "RZT7K7ROYzxV"
      },
      "source": [
        "### 3c. Ratings - duplicates, remove 0s, keep only valid users/books"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "metadata": {
        "colab": {
          "base_uri": "https://localhost:8080/"
        },
        "id": "VapmG3soYzxV",
        "outputId": "43662a8a-944f-4c32-b553-d447e758f697"
      },
      "source": [
        "ratings = (b_ratings.drop(columns='ingestion_timestamp')\n",
        "                    .rename(columns={'User-ID': 'user_id', 'ISBN': 'isbn', 'Book-Rating': 'rating'}))\n",
        "note('ratings: bronze', ratings)\n",
        "\n",
        "ratings['user_id'] = pd.to_numeric(ratings['user_id'], errors='coerce')\n",
        "ratings['rating']  = pd.to_numeric(ratings['rating'], errors='coerce')\n",
        "ratings['isbn']    = clean_text(ratings['isbn']).str.upper()\n",
        "ratings = ratings.dropna(subset=['user_id', 'isbn', 'rating'])\n",
        "ratings = ratings.astype({'user_id': 'int64', 'rating': 'int64'})\n",
        "\n",
        "ratings = ratings.drop_duplicates()\n",
        "ratings = ratings.drop_duplicates(subset=['user_id', 'isbn'], keep='last')  # one rating per user-book pair\n",
        "note('ratings: after removing duplicates', ratings)\n",
        "\n",
        "ratings = ratings[ratings['rating'].between(1, 10)]\n",
        "note('ratings: explicit only (1-10)', ratings)\n",
        "\n",
        "ratings = ratings[ratings['isbn'].isin(books['isbn']) & ratings['user_id'].isin(users['user_id'])]\n",
        "note('ratings: book and user both exist', ratings)"
      ],
      "execution_count": 44,
      "outputs": [
        {
          "output_type": "stream",
          "name": "stdout",
          "text": [
            "ratings: bronze                                          1,149,780\n",
            "ratings: after removing duplicates                       1,149,780\n",
            "ratings: explicit only (1-10)                              433,671\n",
            "ratings: book and user both exist                          383,843\n"
          ]
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "metadata": {
        "id": "oLP1sZenYzxW"
      },
      "source": [
        "### 3d. Minimum-activity threshold\n",
        "\n",
        "**Chosen threshold: every user must have ≥ 10 ratings and every book must have ≥ 10 ratings.**\n",
        "\n",
        "Justification from the EDA: the median user and the median book have only 1.0 explicit rating(s), so most rows carry almost no information about similarity - two books rated by 1-2 people cannot be compared reliably with cosine similarity. A threshold of 10 removes this noise and makes the matrix much denser, while still leaving 1,820 users and 2,030 books (enough to make varied recommendations). Higher thresholds (20, 50) left too few books; lower ones (2, 5) left the matrix almost as sparse as before.\n",
        "\n",
        "The filter is applied **repeatedly** until it is stable, because removing users can push a book below 10 ratings and vice-versa."
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "metadata": {
        "colab": {
          "base_uri": "https://localhost:8080/"
        },
        "id": "IiV-AIaGYzxW",
        "outputId": "2a1dd95a-7cdd-4964-d6ee-fb6ff687c337"
      },
      "source": [
        "MIN_USER_RATINGS = 10\n",
        "MIN_BOOK_RATINGS = 10\n",
        "\n",
        "while True:\n",
        "    user_counts = ratings['user_id'].value_counts()\n",
        "    book_counts = ratings['isbn'].value_counts()\n",
        "    keep = (ratings['user_id'].map(user_counts) >= MIN_USER_RATINGS) & \\\n",
        "           (ratings['isbn'].map(book_counts) >= MIN_BOOK_RATINGS)\n",
        "    if keep.all():\n",
        "        break\n",
        "    ratings = ratings[keep]\n",
        "note(f'ratings: users >= {MIN_USER_RATINGS} and books >= {MIN_BOOK_RATINGS} ratings', ratings)\n",
        "\n",
        "# keep only the users and books that are still in the ratings table\n",
        "users = users[users['user_id'].isin(ratings['user_id'])]\n",
        "books = books[books['isbn'].isin(ratings['isbn'])]\n",
        "print(f'\\nRemaining: {users.shape[0]:,} users, {books.shape[0]:,} books, {len(ratings):,} ratings')"
      ],
      "execution_count": 45,
      "outputs": [
        {
          "output_type": "stream",
          "name": "stdout",
          "text": [
            "ratings: users >= 10 and books >= 10 ratings                41,469\n",
            "\n",
            "Remaining: 1,820 users, 2,030 books, 41,469 ratings\n"
          ]
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "metadata": {
        "colab": {
          "base_uri": "https://localhost:8080/",
          "height": 331
        },
        "id": "J_WPSgmuYzxW",
        "outputId": "4c6a4466-6070-49db-d412-3f405c1b695e"
      },
      "source": [
        "ratings = ratings.reset_index(drop=True)\n",
        "users   = users.reset_index(drop=True)\n",
        "books   = books.reset_index(drop=True)\n",
        "\n",
        "users.to_parquet('silver/users.parquet', index=False)\n",
        "books.to_parquet('silver/books.parquet', index=False)\n",
        "ratings.to_parquet('silver/ratings.parquet', index=False)\n",
        "\n",
        "pd.DataFrame(log, columns=['step', 'rows'])"
      ],

    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "metadata": {
        "id": "DIl1LBxWYzxW"
      },
      "source": [
        "## Step 4 - Build the Gold layer\n",
        "\n",
        "* `gold/user_book_matrix.npz` - sparse user × book rating matrix (+ `user_index` / `book_index` files that map row/column numbers back to IDs)\n",
        "* `gold/book_lookup.parquet` - isbn, title, author\n",
        "* `gold/user_stats.parquet`, `gold/book_stats.parquet` - average rating and number of ratings"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "metadata": {
        "colab": {
          "base_uri": "https://localhost:8080/"
        },
        "id": "_fkQk9mgYzxW",
        "outputId": "bdd9f0eb-18b0-4410-e2cd-0a361b2c7f90"
      },
      "source": [
        "s_users   = pd.read_parquet('silver/users.parquet')\n",
        "s_books   = pd.read_parquet('silver/books.parquet')\n",
        "s_ratings = pd.read_parquet('silver/ratings.parquet')\n",
        "\n",
        "# integer positions for every user (row) and book (column)\n",
        "user_ids = np.sort(s_ratings['user_id'].unique())\n",
        "isbns    = np.sort(s_ratings['isbn'].unique())\n",
        "user_pos = pd.Series(np.arange(len(user_ids)), index=user_ids)\n",
        "book_pos = pd.Series(np.arange(len(isbns)), index=isbns)\n",
        "\n",
        "R = sparse.csr_matrix(\n",
        "    (s_ratings['rating'].astype(np.float32).values,\n",
        "     (user_pos[s_ratings['user_id']].values, book_pos[s_ratings['isbn']].values)),\n",
        "    shape=(len(user_ids), len(isbns)))\n",
        "\n",
        "sparse.save_npz('gold/user_book_matrix.npz', R)\n",
        "pd.DataFrame({'row': np.arange(len(user_ids)), 'user_id': user_ids}).to_parquet('gold/user_index.parquet', index=False)\n",
        "pd.DataFrame({'col': np.arange(len(isbns)), 'isbn': isbns}).to_parquet('gold/book_index.parquet', index=False)\n",
        "\n",
        "density = R.nnz / (R.shape[0] * R.shape[1]) * 100\n",
        "print(f'Rating matrix: {R.shape[0]:,} users x {R.shape[1]:,} books, {R.nnz:,} ratings, density {density:.3f}%')"
      ],
      "execution_count": 47,
      "outputs": [
        {
          "output_type": "stream",
          "name": "stdout",
          "text": [
            "Rating matrix: 1,820 users x 2,030 books, 41,469 ratings, density 1.122%\n"
          ]
        }
      ]

    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "metadata": {
        "id": "L4WZ1isoYzxW"
      },
      "source": [
        "## Step 5 - Item-based collaborative filtering\n",
        "\n",
        "Idea: two books are similar if the **same users** gave them similar ratings. Each book is a vector of ratings over all users, and we compare books with **cosine similarity** (1 = identical rating pattern, 0 = nothing in common).\n",
        "\n",
        "### 5.1 Load the Gold matrix and transpose it (rows = books, columns = users)"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "metadata": {
        "colab": {
          "base_uri": "https://localhost:8080/"
        },
        "id": "w0bMuH9EYzxW",
        "outputId": "75ed6cd9-5fbc-4a77-ef51-e8eea34013e6"
      },
      "source": [
        "R           = sparse.load_npz('gold/user_book_matrix.npz')\n",
        "user_index  = pd.read_parquet('gold/user_index.parquet')\n",
        "book_index  = pd.read_parquet('gold/book_index.parquet')\n",
        "book_lookup = pd.read_parquet('gold/book_lookup.parquet')\n",
        "book_stats  = pd.read_parquet('gold/book_stats.parquet')\n",
        "\n",
        "item_user = R.T.tocsr()        # rows = books, columns = users\n",
        "print('item-user matrix shape:', item_user.shape)\n",
        "\n",
        "col_isbn  = book_index.sort_values('col')['isbn'].values               # column number -> isbn\n",
        "isbn_col  = {isbn: c for c, isbn in enumerate(col_isbn)}               # isbn -> column number\n",
        "user_row  = dict(zip(user_index['user_id'], user_index['row']))        # user_id -> row number\n",
        "info      = book_lookup.set_index('isbn').reindex(col_isbn)\n",
        "col_title  = info['title'].fillna('(unknown title)').values\n",
        "col_author = info['author'].fillna('(unknown author)').values"
      ],
      "execution_count": 49,
      "outputs": [
        {
          "output_type": "stream",
          "name": "stdout",
          "text": [
            "item-user matrix shape: (2030, 1820)\n"
          ]
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "metadata": {
        "id": "WuEAUraRYzxW"
      },
      "source": [
        "### 5.2 Cosine similarity between books with `NearestNeighbors`"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "metadata": {
        "colab": {
          "base_uri": "https://localhost:8080/"
        },
        "id": "PB42q5gZYzxW",
        "outputId": "0a6ec267-8978-4715-9507-b3e98c024768"
      },
      "source": [
        "K = min(50, item_user.shape[0] - 1)     # neighbours stored per book\n",
        "knn = NearestNeighbors(metric='cosine', algorithm='brute', n_neighbors=K + 1)\n",
        "knn.fit(item_user)\n",
        "\n",
        "distances, neighbours = knn.kneighbors(item_user)   # neighbours of every book\n",
        "similarities = 1 - distances                        # cosine similarity = 1 - cosine distance\n",
        "print('neighbour table:', neighbours.shape)"
      ],
      "execution_count": 50,
      "outputs": [
        {
          "output_type": "stream",
          "name": "stdout",
          "text": [
            "neighbour table: (2030, 51)\n"
          ]
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "metadata": {
        "id": "6thKbk4zYzxX"
      },
      "source": [
        "### 5.3 `similar_books(title)` - the 10 most similar books to a given title"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "metadata": {
        "id": "xkDq0m2iYzxX"
      },
      "source": [
        "def find_book(title):\n",
        "    # Return the isbn for a title (case-insensitive). If several editions match, take the most-rated one.\n",
        "    t = title.strip().lower()\n",
        "    titles_lower = book_lookup['title'].str.lower()\n",
        "    matches = book_lookup[titles_lower == t]\n",
        "    if matches.empty:\n",
        "        matches = book_lookup[titles_lower.str.contains(t, regex=False, na=False)]\n",
        "    if matches.empty:\n",
        "        raise ValueError(f'No book found matching \"{title}\"')\n",
        "    matches = matches.merge(book_stats[['isbn', 'num_ratings']], on='isbn')\n",
        "    return matches.sort_values('num_ratings', ascending=False)['isbn'].iloc[0]\n",
        "\n",
        "\n",
        "def similar_books(title, n=10):\n",
        "    c = isbn_col[find_book(title)]\n",
        "    print(f'Books similar to: {col_title[c]} - {col_author[c]}')\n",
        "    seen_titles = {col_title[c].lower()}\n",
        "    rows = []\n",
        "    for j, sim in zip(neighbours[c], similarities[c]):\n",
        "        if j == c or col_title[j].lower() in seen_titles:   # skip itself and other editions of it\n",
        "            continue\n",
        "        seen_titles.add(col_title[j].lower())\n",
        "        rows.append({'title': col_title[j], 'author': col_author[j], 'similarity': round(float(sim), 3)})\n",
        "        if len(rows) == n:\n",
        "            break\n",
        "    return pd.DataFrame(rows, index=range(1, len(rows) + 1))"
      ],
      "execution_count": 51,
      "outputs": []
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "metadata": {
        "colab": {
          "base_uri": "https://localhost:8080/",
          "height": 381
        },
        "id": "-zzkSZyfYzxX",
        "outputId": "fb8b4a3b-9777-43f4-86a6-a8d3a9beb1d9"
      },
      "source": [
        "most_rated_title = book_stats.sort_values('num_ratings', ascending=False)['title'].iloc[0]\n",
        "similar_books(most_rated_title)"
      ],
      "execution_count": 52,
      "outputs": [
        {

            ],
            "text/html": [
              "\n",

    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "metadata": {
        "id": "kBW_IEa5YzxY"
      },
      "source": [
        "### 5.4 `recommend(user_id, n=10)`\n",
        "\n",
        "1. Take the books this user rated highly (rating ≥ 8; if they have none, use their highest-rated books).\n",
        "2. For each of those books, collect its most similar books.\n",
        "3. Score each candidate as **Σ similarity × user's rating of the liked book** — books similar to several of the user's favourites, or to books they loved, rank higher.\n",
        "4. Remove books the user has already rated (including other editions with the same title) and return the top *n*."
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "metadata": {
        "id": "wTyjtLKAYzxY"
      },
      "source": [
        "HIGH_RATING = 8\n",
        "\n",
        "def liked_books(user_id, min_rating=HIGH_RATING):\n",
        "    row = R[user_row[user_id]]\n",
        "    rated = pd.DataFrame({'col': row.indices, 'rating': row.data.astype(int)})\n",
        "    liked = rated[rated['rating'] >= min_rating]\n",
        "    if liked.empty:                                   # fall back to the user's top-rated books\n",
        "        liked = rated[rated['rating'] == rated['rating'].max()]\n",
        "    return rated, liked.sort_values('rating', ascending=False)\n",
        "\n",
        "\n",
        "def recommend(user_id, n=10):\n",
        "    if user_id not in user_row:\n",
        "        raise ValueError(f'User {user_id} is not in the Gold data (too few ratings).')\n",
        "    rated, liked = liked_books(user_id)\n",
        "    already_read_cols   = set(rated['col'])\n",
        "    already_read_titles = {col_title[c].lower() for c in already_read_cols}\n",
        "\n",
        "    scores = defaultdict(float)\n",
        "    for c, user_rating in zip(liked['col'], liked['rating']):\n",
        "        for j, sim in zip(neighbours[c], similarities[c]):\n",
        "            if j == c or j in already_read_cols or sim <= 0:\n",
        "                continue\n",
        "            scores[j] += sim * user_rating\n",
        "\n",
        "    ranked = sorted(scores.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1], reverse=True)\n",
        "    rows, seen = [], set(already_read_titles)\n",
        "    for j, score in ranked:\n",
        "        t = col_title[j].lower()\n",
        "        if t in seen:                                     # skip other editions / duplicates\n",
        "            continue\n",
        "        seen.add(t)\n",
        "        rows.append({'recommended_title': col_title[j], 'author': col_author[j], 'score': round(float(score), 3)})\n",
        "        if len(rows) == n:\n",
        "            break\n",
        "    return pd.DataFrame(rows, index=range(1, len(rows) + 1))"
      ],
      "execution_count": 54,
      "outputs": []
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "metadata": {
        "id": "jsBnXwePYzxY"
      },
      "source": [
        "## Step 6 - Demo and sanity check\n",
        "\n",
        "We pick three different users (a heavy reader, a medium reader and a light reader) and show the books they rated highly **next to** their recommendations."
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "metadata": {
        "colab": {
          "base_uri": "https://localhost:8080/"
        },
        "id": "q-sQ-07KYzxY",
        "outputId": "dc067428-8f2f-4add-8efb-faa2ba9d8e6b"
      },
      "source": [
        "user_stats = pd.read_parquet('gold/user_stats.parquet')\n",
        "ranked_users = user_stats.sort_values('num_ratings', ascending=False).reset_index(drop=True)\n",
        "demo_users = [int(ranked_users.loc[i, 'user_id']) for i in [0, len(ranked_users) // 2, len(ranked_users) - 1]]\n",
        "# You can also pick your own, e.g. demo_users = [11676, 98391, 153662]\n",
        "print('Demo users:', demo_users)"
      ],
      "execution_count": 55,
      "outputs": [
        {
          "output_type": "stream",
          "name": "stdout",
          "text": [
            "Demo users: [11676, 192245, 805]\n"
          ]
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "metadata": {
        "colab": {
          "base_uri": "https://localhost:8080/",
          "height": 1000
        },
        "id": "23zZRj11YzxY",
        "outputId": "5a7eaf45-b36d-4716-ec85-2ec602c684c8"
      },
      "source": [
        "def show_user(user_id, n=10):\n",
        "    rated, liked = liked_books(user_id)\n",
        "    favourites = pd.DataFrame({\n",
        "        'rated_highly': [col_title[c] for c in liked['col']],\n",
        "        'their_rating': liked['rating'].values,\n",
        "    }).head(n)\n",
        "    favourites.index = range(1, len(favourites) + 1)\n",
        "    recs = recommend(user_id, n)\n",
        "    print(f'\\n================ USER {user_id}  ({len(rated)} ratings, {len(liked)} liked) ================')\n",
        "    side_by_side = pd.concat([favourites, recs[['recommended_title', 'score']]], axis=1)\n",
        "    side_by_side['their_rating'] = side_by_side['their_rating'].map(lambda x: '' if pd.isna(x) else int(x))\n",
        "    display(side_by_side.fillna(''))\n",
        "\n",
        "for uid in demo_users:\n",
        "    show_user(uid)"
      ],

        "### Sanity check (write your own observations)\n",
        "\n",
        "* **User 11676:** liked mostly contemporary fiction and drama books; recommendations are similar mainstream bestsellers - does that make sense? Yes, because they have a high number of ratings and represent highly correlated reading preferences.\n",
        "* **User 192245:** liked mystery, drama and general fiction; recommendations are highly relevant because they match highly co-rated popular titles.\n",
        "* **User 805:** liked thriller and popular suspense novels; recommendations are aligned with major mystery authors.\n",
        "* `similar_books()` for *The Lovely Bones: A Novel* returned books by Alice Sebold (such as *Lucky : A Memoir*) and other popular contemporary thrillers/dramas like *The Da Vinci Code* and *The Pilot's Wife*, which shows the similarity is highly meaningful.\n",
        "\n",
        "Limitations: only users and books with ≥ 10 ratings can be served (cold-start problem); popular books appear often because they share many raters."
